name: Kingdom of Prussia

areaKm2.note: world_1815 "Prussia" polygons = 215,200 + 41,000 km2 plus slivers (~256,700) on the sphere; Prussia in 1866 was ~280,000 km2, plus Schleswig (~9,000) under Prussian administration.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1865 = 20,421k (1866 annual value 24,342k includes the annexations of late 1866). Plus Schleswig under Prussian administration (~0.4M) from 1865.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) Germany 1860 = 14.5%, 1870 = 14.8% (towns 5,000+ convention lower than national definitions). COW upop 1865 = 1,020k (cities 100k+) = 5%.

activePersonnel.note: Mobilised line army incl. recalled reservists, June 1866. Austro-Prussian War page: Prussia 437,262 deployed (Clodfelter 2017 p. 182) incl. Landwehr; Moltke's field army of 285,000 moved over five railway lines; Koeniggraetz 220,984 (Prussian General Staff via battle page). COW milper 1865 = 216,000 (peace).

trainedReserves.note: Landwehr and Ersatz formations: the difference between the 437,262 deployed and the ~300,000-335,000 line army, plus Landwehr II not called.

mobilizationRatio.note: Franco-Prussian War infobox: Germany deployed 1,494,412 in 1870-71 (Clodfelter p. 184) from ~40M (3.7%) within months; 1866 Prussia deployed 437,262 of 20M (2.2%) in weeks. Total-war ceiling ~6%.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: 9 corps and the Guard at war strength (~25 battalions of ~1,000 per corps) plus fortress and depot infantry of the line army.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Dreyse needle gun, the only breech-loader of the war; three to five rounds a minute prone

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: 3-year conscripts and recent reservists, company-column tactics

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Dreyse rifles

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: forester-recruited marksmen

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: heavy horses

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: held back in 1866

count.note: Dragoons, hussars and uhlans (~32 regiments) at ~600 each.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: lances and sabres

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: reconnaissance weak in 1866, reformed for 1870

count.note: Field guns of the field army and depots; the page says Prussia had replaced up to 60% of its smoothbores with the C64 rifled breech-loader by 1866.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: mixed C64 Krupp breech-loaders and smoothbore 12-pdrs

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: artillery held too far back at Koeniggraetz (battle page: 66 guns of the corps artillery too far to the rear)

count.note: Educated guess: two small ironclads (Arminius, Prinz Adalbert) and the Arcona-class screw frigates; most of the navy was overseas or laid up.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: small modern ships

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: young navy, few trained officers

count.note: Educated guess: screw gunboats and corvettes.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: young navy

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Moltke and the General Staff; railway concentration and converging armies at Koeniggraetz

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75. Evidence: territorial corps with regimental identity; conscript army

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75. Evidence: victory over Denmark in 1864; war unpopular at home until the first victories

weapons.note: Anchor: between 6 (1805) and 7 (1905). Evidence: breech-loading Dreyse and C64 breech-loading Krupp guns

armor.note: Anchor: 6 (none / cuirass). Evidence: cuirassiers; no land armour

ships.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: two small turret/broadside ironclads

fortification.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: polygonal Prussian fortresses on the Rhine (Koblenz, Cologne)

logistics.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: five railway lines to the front, field army concentrated in 25 days (Austro-Prussian War page)

communications.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: telegraph links from Berlin to army headquarters

isr.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: cavalry lost contact with the Austrian army before Koeniggraetz

air.note: No military aircraft before 1911; balloons, where used, are counted under ISR.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID) Germany 1865 = 2,821, 1866 = 2,823. Prussia (Rhineland and Silesian industry, poor eastern provinces) close to the German mean.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: COW NMC v7 milex (thousands of pounds) 1865 = 5,950, 1866 = 6,268; against a national product of ~250-280M pounds that is ~2.5% in peace; the war was financed partly from the 1865-66 reserves, mid includes mobilisation costs.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: Rhineland-Westphalia and Silesia coal and iron; industry and crafts ~25% of output.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: grain exports from the eastern provinces.

annualCohort.note: Analogue: France 1805 snapshot ratio, males reaching military age = 0.95-1.15% of population per year (Elting ch. 9), applied to this population. Prussia called ~63,000 conscripts a year, a fraction of the class.

artillery.note: Educated guess: Krupp and state arsenal field-gun output per year.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: Prussia bought its ironclads abroad.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: Prussian state and provincial chaussees.

railKm.note: CHAT (https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta) railline Germany 1866 = 14,861 km for the whole of Germany; Prussia's share by population (20/38M) and area ~0.5-0.57.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Koenigsberg, Danzig, Stettin, Swinemuende, Memel, Kiel (administered).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: about a third of the German registered fleet (CHAT Germany 1866 = 930k tons, https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta) sailed from Prussian Baltic ports; x1.5 to deadweight.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses of the Prussian provinces.

homeDefense.note: 1.1 row: familiar terrain, Rhine fortresses; open plains.

notes: Snapshot = Kingdom of Prussia in mid-June 1866 after mobilisation. Territory and population = Prussia plus Schleswig under Prussian administration; North German allies and Italy (200,000) excluded; includes is empty. Personnel: line army incl. recalled reservists = active (the mobilisation was complete by the snapshot date); Landwehr and Ersatz = trainedReserves. Strengths from the Austro-Prussian War page (Clodfelter 2017 p. 182: 437,262) and the Koeniggraetz page (220,984 at the battle); branch split is a reconstruction (grade C).
